# Third-party source artifacts

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

This directory pins reviewed third-party plugin artifacts used by the dsh-teacher distribution. They are project build inputs, not per-machine installation files: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` declares them as dependencies and mounts them in its shipped profile, so source launches and the Windows EXE need no separate `dsh plugin add` step.

The Web bundle also pins `@huanlin/dsh-plugin-better-sidebar-plugin-office` 0.1.2 from npm. That AGPL-3.0 package registers DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX viewers with the built-in better-sidebar file registry.

<a id="configuration-and-migration"></a>
## Configuration and migration

AnySearch works without a key, within the remote service's anonymous limits. The [Web bundle](../packages/bundle/web-app/README.md#built-in-web-search) owns optional credential, endpoint, and per-search result-cap configuration, provider selection, and the disclosure of outbound queries and extraction URLs. The installer contains the plugin, not the search service or a registered account.

Executable code ships with the repository and EXE; machine-specific state does not. Bot credentials, QQ settings, cron jobs, skill files, MCP configuration, Univer documents, worktrees, and downloaded resource caches remain under `DSH_HOME` or the selected workspace. Configure bots through **Settings → Plugins → Connected Platforms**. Configure speech-recognition and image-generation routes under **Settings → Models → Service access**, then assign each supported model under **Use cases**; browser voice input, QQ voice messages, and image-generation tools use those assignments. Provider API keys use the credential store, while generated-image history, the gallery, and template caches use `~/.dsh/dsh-imagegen`; recordings, reference images, and prompts are sent to the selected providers. Manage skills under **Settings → Skills**, and manage MCP servers under **Settings → MCP** or through `dsh-panel mcp`. In the installed Windows desktop, a bot's **Choose directory** action uses the in-app Host directory browser; it does not require a Windows system folder dialog. The `dsh-im/cordis.patch.yml.example` file remains only as a reference for deployments that need an explicit `qq.outboundMediaRoots` override.

The built-in Univer row sets `telemetry: false`. Without `UNIVER_LICENSE`, the Univer Viewer opens in the upstream limited evaluation mode, including its watermark and feature limits. Supply a valid license through `UNIVER_LICENSE` for licensed features; the artifact contains no development-license fallback. Some Slide layout checks, SVG text measurement, and screenshot operations also require a local Chrome or Chromium executable, selected explicitly with `UNIVER_RENDER_BROWSER` when automatic discovery is insufficient.

Windows desktop control starts by default when its runtime is available; persisted user values remain effective, while the generic **Plugin configuration** tab does not expose this built-in integration. The installed x64 desktop supplies its own private runtime, so users do not install Python, Windows-MCP, or another MCP row. Full access unlocks all twenty pinned tools without extra desktop approval; other modes expose thirteen desktop tools with per-call approval. The [Windows-MCP package](../packages/mcp/windows-mcp/README.md) owns the complete catalog and session permission rules.

To migrate a machine, install the new EXE or clone and build the repository, then copy the required `DSH_HOME`, `~/.dsh/dsh-imagegen`, and workspace data separately. Do not reinstall the built-in integrations into the generated user profile; remove separately installed image-generation or Windows-MCP rows before starting the built-in release because duplicate rows can register duplicate tools and sidebar entries.

## Bot workspaces

New bots on all nine platforms under **Settings → Plugins → Connected Platforms** default to the Host user's desktop. Electron supplies the operating system's desktop path through `DSH_DESKTOP_DIR`, including OneDrive and relocated desktops. Source and standalone Web launches use `<home>/Desktop` unless `DSH_DESKTOP_DIR` supplies another absolute path. An explicit `workspace` in a platform's IM configuration takes precedence over the default. Existing saved bot workspaces remain unchanged; **Choose directory** saves a replacement for that bot.

The [IM patch](../patches/xmanrui-dsh-im@4.11.0.patch) owns this distribution default through its `desktop-workspace.mjs` Host entry. The upstream controllers still own workspace persistence and bot lifecycle; Office configuration is unchanged. The [decision record](../.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-09-01-im-bot-desktop-workspaces.md) explains path ownership and preservation of saved values.

## Verification

The real shipped-composition browser lane asserts that all client modules are in the module graph. It also pins the four image-generation tools, Host-level `cron_*`, `qq_send_local_file`, thirteen `univer_*` tools, and Windows-MCP's runtime-aware default with saved opt-outs, while the Models lane rejects separate image and Voice model cards, configures supplier routes, and saves image and speech assignments under Use cases. The voice-input lane sends browser recordings through that supplier assignment. The QQ workspace-picker lane opens a seeded bot's directory action, confirms that speech settings are absent from the QQ page, and snapshots the in-app listing returned by the real Host backend; a Host integration test also requires QQ WAV attachments to delegate to the shared speech runtime. The desktop payload gate separately requires the image-generation Host and Client bundles, built-in template snapshot, and license; the Univer Viewer, Gateway, workers, skills, commercial resource manifest, and Windows x64 native bindings; and the embedded CPython executable, Windows-MCP metadata, and representative Python native modules.

<a id="artifact-notes"></a>
## Artifact notes

The AnySearch archive is compiled from the supplied 0.1.4 source with its frozen lockfile and retains its MIT license, compiled modules, declarations, bundle patch, README pair, and linked documentation assets. Its SHA-256 is `08d583857ec3b9307157f45c68bfbc91f7863a54c143a0f3e34079afff578079`. The [compatibility patch](../patches/anysearch-anysearch-dsh@0.1.4.patch) removes the upstream global `web_fetch` fallback because DSH session presets own that tool, and projects the credential reference, endpoint, and per-search result cap through a live DSH settings section whose values are snapshotted per operation. Scoped dependency overrides bind its pre-1.0 peer declarations to the current workspace services. The shipped-composition and AnySearch integration tests exercise those APIs, the search-session snapshot pins model-visible results, and the desktop payload gate requires its license and every runtime module.

The image-generation archive is a runtime-only repack of upstream npm release 1.5.1. It retains the unchanged compiled Host and Client bundles, bundled 441-case template snapshot, package metadata, bundle patch, README, and Apache-2.0 license; it omits the 50 MB release's screenshots, demonstration video, non-runtime TypeScript sources, and source map. The [image-generation compatibility patch](../patches/dickpy-dsh-imagegen@1.5.1.patch) removes the separate Models card, consumes the image assignment and exact Service access route for every task, resolves its credential through the shared store, dispatches OpenAI Images, DashScope, or MiniMax formats, and updates Host and Client configuration guidance to the unified location. The official npm tarball SHA-256 is `f95c6ac0099d2dc958e07efb2a4a35dd036c832db30d6e3d37fb63b916bda820`; the reviewed runtime repack SHA-256 is `dc0877229e38fbd19d716654460a0f0a4346992e37318fb8e48853f34a29ec51`.

The official dsh-im npm archive contains its source and MIT license; its SHA-256 is `0a5b6e1018d238b4fba39be9c27b6d6acad177b496f4ee8699bbc8526c74c603`. The distribution patch preserves desktop workspace and shared QQ speech behavior, uses the release's modern same-process Host adapter, and reports an expired Weixin scan token as an actionable re-scan error. The cron archive contains compiled `lib/` output, its bundle patch, README, and MIT license. The skill/MCP archive is the upstream MIT release artifact; the repository compatibility patch updates its client injections and session lookup for this DSH revision. Its SHA-256 is `5e8523cfea0c4ca2cf7a71600f6eaa67655258b1ddce317e5c06f0658620737a`.

The Windows runtime assembly pins the official CPython 3.14.7 AMD64 embedded archive, the Windows-MCP 0.8.5 wheel, and the supplied project's complete Python source archive by SHA-256 in `windows-mcp/runtime.json`. The wheel supplies distribution metadata; `windows-mcp/source.py` installs the reviewed source over it and verifies all twenty tool signatures. The complete binary-only wheel closure is hash-pinned in `windows-mcp/requirements.lock`. Reviewed patches replace `fuzzywuzzy` with the compatible MIT `TheFuzz` API and correlate Scrape sampling with its calling DSH tool. `fuzzywuzzy`, `Levenshtein`, and `python-Levenshtein` stay excluded. Packaging requires real stdio discovery and `Wait`, plus FastMCP sampling, DOM, opt-out, and fallback smokes. The [source-parity decision](../.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-09-01-windows-mcp-source-parity.md) owns the source and patch policy.

The Univer archive is rebuilt from the supplied 0.2.12 source. The rebuild removes the source's embedded development-license fallback and passes only the runtime `UNIVER_LICENSE` value into its Viewer, Gateway, render process, and unit-content worker. The [Viewer source patch](dsh-univer-office/viewer-license.patch) accepts an empty runtime license string and leaves license validation and evaluation limits to Univer; malformed configuration still fails. Its SHA-256 is `c1ee7a6911aa0099a4dd9c84d158b4d57d75255b78a64369a89aa87239ef4498`. The wrapper declares Apache-2.0, but its executable closure includes three external `@univerjs-pro/*` runtime roots and 90 separately licensed build-time modules that its build script inlines into the artifacts: 79 under `@univerjs-pro/*` and 11 under `@univer-cli/*`. The compiled tarball does not carry those modules' individual manifests or notices; the generated notices therefore list every declared identity and pin their declaration digest. Building or distributing the repository requires appropriate [Univer Pro licensing and distribution rights](https://docs.univer.ai/guides/pro/license), including authorization for those bundled modules. Update any pinned archive only after reviewing its executable closure, provenance, licenses, local compatibility changes, native payloads, and shipped-composition behavior together.
